title: HVAC Service Call Work Order
subtitle: Residential HVAC Service Call: connects authorized scope to results.
description: HVAC Service Call Work Order covers heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone. The home-service coordinator records Residential HVAC Service Call authorized tasks, materials, results, and changes. HVAC Service Call Work Order keeps Residential HVAC Service Call exceptions visible until the home-service coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use HVAC Service Call Work Order at residence, equipment location, thermostat zone, and exterior unit area. Document heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone identity before Residential HVAC Service Call begins. Compare heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone findings with stated Residential HVAC Service Call criteria; route unresolved Residential HVAC Service Call issues to qualified HVAC technician. For HVAC Service Call Work Order, confirm requirements for Residential HVAC Service Call. Ask qualified HVAC technician to review Residential HVAC Service Call conditions beyond the home-service coordinator's role.

sections.title: Residential work exception and changes
sections.guidance: Stop Residential HVAC Service Call at any scope or cost limit; honor home-service coordinator access and safety boundaries.

blocks.label: Do not proceed without control
blocks.guidance: Stop normal processing when a fuel, electrical, refrigerant, water, access, or safe-operation concern remains. Protect heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone; document the Residential HVAC Service Call notification and await qualified HVAC technician direction.

blocks.label: Conditions requiring stop or renewed authorization
items: Gas odor, combustion, damaged conductor, or water damage
System cannot be tested or restored safely
blocks.guidance: For Residential HVAC Service Call, identify affected heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone scope; ask home-service coordinator to document the Residential HVAC Service Call immediate control before continuing.
